speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to begin my assessment, how many years has your cough persisted, and do you currently smoke or have any history of smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The duration of 11 years, the production of copious thick, purulent sputum, morning predominance, and recurrent bronchitis in a non-smoker are classic indicators. To confirm this, I need to see your chest imaging and sputum analysis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT; REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture_and_Sensitivity.
